Saturn, the card's planet, is good at looking at the numbers calmly.

With earnings, it might mean slowly planning an exit from a well-paid job that bores you, with savings behind you. With possessions, a clear-out that feels a bit sad for a day and then much lighter. With self-worth, noticing you've been charging too little because you were grateful to be asked. Go through your regular payments and cancel one you're keeping out of habit.
2.reversed:
Holding on to money or things out of fear is the usual shape of this card reversed in the second house. The job's draining you and you stay for the pay. The house is full and you can't face sorting it. Or it goes the other way, and you spend to fill the gap the card's pointing at, buying small comforts to cover a larger dissatisfaction.

Venus rules this house and likes things pleasant, and the sextile with Pisces is an opening that only works if you use it. Left alone, it just keeps things comfortable. Where it shows is in your bank statements, in a cupboard of things bought and never used, and in how you talk about your own value at work. Look through your recent spending and circle anything you bought to cheer yourself up.

3.upright:
Conversations run their course like anything else. The third house is the everyday talk of your life, the messages and phone calls, your brothers and sisters, the neighbours, the short trips you make without thinking, and whatever you're learning. With this card here, one of those exchanges has gone stale. It could be a group chat you've stopped enjoying, a weekly call with a sibling that's turned into a report on nothing, or a course you signed up for and no longer care about.

Gemini, the house's natural sign, squares Pisces. Both are mutable, both change their minds, and the square makes it hard to settle anything in words. Water and air don't clash, and they don't naturally understand each other either, so the feeling in this card and the words you have for it tend not to line up. You might start to explain why you're stepping back from something and hear yourself giving a practical reason that isn't the real one. The Moon has its joy in this house, which suggests feelings are welcome here even when they're hard to say. It's worth trying to say the real reason.

With a sibling, it could be a gentle change in how often you talk, with no falling-out needed. In study, it's dropping a subject you took up for somebody else. Locally, the café, the route to work, the neighbourhood you've always used might have gone flat. Take a different way to somewhere you go often and see what you notice.
3.reversed:
When this card's reversed in the third house, the leaving tends to stay in words. You talk about quitting the course, about moving suburbs, about stepping back from your sister's dramas, and you talk about it so much it starts to stand in for doing it. Mercury rules this house, and with the square from Pisces it can keep you circling a decision in conversation for a long time.

The other version is the unsaid goodbye, dropping out of a group chat or a class with no explanation and leaving people confused. With siblings, an old pattern of who speaks for whom might need changing. In study, you might be half-committed to something you should either finish or drop. Say the true reason for stepping back to one person, in plain words, and leave it at that.

4.upright:
Home is the ground under everything else, and the fourth house covers it literally, the house or flat you live in, your family, your parents, where you come from and where you go to be private. Drawn here, this card is about outgrowing some part of that. It might be the actual place, a flat that suited you once. It might be a role in the family, being the peacemaker or the one who hosts. Sometimes it's a way of thinking about where you belong that stopped being true a while ago.

The trine between Pisces and Cancer, this house's natural sign, and the shared element mean the feeling comes through clearly and strongly. You'll know exactly how sad it is to leave, and water on water makes that louder. The practical side is harder. Saturn is badly placed in Cancer, in its detriment, which means the card's steadiness struggles in this house, so putting in a firm boundary with a parent, or actually signing a lease somewhere new, is heavy going. It's one of the angles of the chart, too, and changes here tend to be felt through the rest of your life.

With a parent, this might be accepting that they won't become the parent you wanted. At home, clearing out a room or a cupboard that's full of an old life. With a family tradition, letting it lapse without a fight. Choose one object in your home that belongs to a past version of you and pass it on to someone.
4.reversed:
The fourth house reversed can keep you in a home long after it's stopped feeling like one. You stay in the family house to look after it. You keep the Sunday lunch going that nobody enjoys. You keep your childhood bedroom exactly as it was. With water on water and Saturn in detriment in Cancer, the pull backward is strong and the will to say enough is thin.

Sometimes it shows as the opposite, moving flat after flat and never unpacking, because settling would mean admitting you've left the old place for good. Family members may lean on you in ways that are hard to refuse. Sleep can get restless. Have one honest conversation with a relative about something you've been doing out of duty, and ask whether they even want you to keep doing it.

5.upright:
Fun can go stale, and the fifth house is where you'd notice. Romance, hobbies, the creative work you do for love, children if you have them, the ways you play. The card here points to a pleasure that's become a routine. The band you've been in for years. A dating app you keep opening. The Friday night that's the same every Friday. A creative project you're only finishing because you said you would.

Saturn doesn't do well in this house. Its natural sign is Leo, where Saturn sits in detriment, so the card's sobriety runs straight against the house's love of warmth and show. Pisces and Leo are a quincunx apart with nothing in common, and water and fire are opposed. There's a real tension between wanting a good time and noticing that the good time isn't very good any more. Venus rejoices in this house and she'd happily keep the party going, which makes it easy to ignore how tired of it you are.

In romance, this could be ending something light that was fun at first and has turned into a habit. With a creative hobby, putting down one project so you've got energy for another that actually excites you. With children, dropping an activity you push them to that neither of you enjoys. Cancel one standing plan and use the free evening for something you've never tried.
5.reversed:
Chasing a kind of fun you've outgrown is one way this card goes when it's reversed here. The same nights out, the same type of person on dates, the same hobby you're no longer much good at and don't really enjoy. Saturn in detriment in Leo can't call time on it, and the opposed elements leave you bored and restless at once.

Other times it's the opposite, and you give up on pleasure altogether, stop making things, stop dating, and decide you're too old for it. Either way it shows in your mood at weekends and in a creative streak that's gone quiet. If there are children around, you may find yourself impatient with their play. Do one thing purely for enjoyment, badly if need be, and don't turn it into a project.

6.upright:
Same breakfast, same run, same way of organising the week. The sixth house is the daily grind, the actual hours of the working day, the chores, the routines that keep your body going, what you eat and when you sleep and whether you get outside. With this card here, a routine has stopped doing its job. You're still doing it, faithfully, and it's stopped leaving you any better off.

Virgo, this house's natural sign, sits opposite Pisces. So the card brings the other end of the axis into your daily life, the side that's fed up with lists and wants to let go. The opposition is a pull toward balance, and in the sixth that usually means a looser routine with some air in it. Water and earth get on, which helps, because this needn't be dramatic. You can change a routine a piece at a time. Mars has its joy here, so once you've decided, there's energy for the practical work. I've seen people draw this card in the sixth and realise their whole health routine was built for someone they used to be.

At work, it might be handing over daily tasks you've done so long you could do them asleep. With your body, dropping a fitness habit that's become a chore for something gentler or more fun. In the evenings, noticing which bit of the routine is really avoidance. Change one fixed part of your day and keep the change going for a fortnight.
6.reversed:
Reversed in the sixth house, this card can look like someone doing the same exhausting routine every day and calling it discipline. You know the schedule's wearing you down. You keep it because stopping feels like letting yourself go. Virgo, this house's natural sign, sits opposite Pisces, and here the longing for rest ends up on the far side of the chart, ignored.

Or the routine falls apart altogether, meals skipped, sleep all over the place, the to-do list abandoned, which is the same card from the other side. At work, it shows in tasks you do on autopilot and resent. In the body, as tiredness you keep overriding. Pick the part of your day that drains you most and find one way to make it shorter.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person across from you. Your partner or spouse, a business partner, a client you work closely with, and sometimes the one person you're always arguing with. It's an angle, so what happens here is visible. The card in this house is about a one-to-one arrangement that's reached its edge. Nobody's done anything wrong. It just isn't enough any more, or the terms you agreed to at the start don't fit who either of you has become.

Saturn is exalted in Libra, this house's natural sign. It's welcomed here and at its most fair-minded, which means the card can do its difficult work in this house with real decency. Whatever you decide, whether that's to leave or to change the terms and stay, you're likely to do it honestly and carefully. The strain comes from the quincunx. Pisces and Libra have nothing in common, and the card's quiet, private longing doesn't fit the house's wish to keep things balanced and pleasant. Water and air have to be introduced, so you may find it hard to put into words for the other person what you already feel.

In a relationship, it could be a frank conversation about whether you both still want the same life. In business, ending a partnership or a contract properly, with the paperwork done well. With a close friend you've relied on one-to-one, admitting you've drifted apart. Write down what would have to change for the arrangement to feel right, and share it with the other person.
7.reversed:
With this card reversed in the seventh house, a partnership can go into limbo. Neither of you leaves and neither of you really stays. You share a house and not much else, or a business where you've stopped consulting each other. Saturn is exalted in Libra, the sign that belongs to this house, and it's good at keeping agreements, even ones that have outlived their point.

Sometimes it's a repeat, going back to someone you'd left, or finding a new partner who's the old one with a different name. It shows up in contracts you keep renewing without reading, and in arguments that go round in circles. Clients or a business partner may sense you've checked out before you've said a word. Say the thing you've both been avoiding, calmly, and agree on when you'll come back to it.

8.upright:
Shared money, debts, the joint account, an inheritance, and intimacy, sex included. The eighth house covers what you share with someone at close range, and it's also where endings live. So this is a card of leaving in a house of endings. Pisces and Scorpio, this house's natural sign, are in trine and share an element, so the card goes in deep and meets no resistance, and water on water turns every feeling up.

What you're likely to feel is a quiet ending in something intimate. It may be the way you and a partner are close, which has become a habit more than a meeting. It may be a financial tie, money lent to a relative that you've accepted you won't see again, or a joint arrangement you've outgrown. Grief can surface here too, sometimes old grief, for a person or a time you thought you'd finished with. Mars, the traditional ruler of Scorpio, gives the house some nerve, so you'll probably face this head on. Saturn doesn't hurry, and that suits the eighth, where things need to end properly.

With a partner, it could be an honest talk about intimacy and what's gone missing. With money, separating finances, or closing an account you've kept open out of sentiment. With a loss, letting yourself grieve something you've been brave about for a long time. Find one shared financial tie that no longer makes sense and start the paperwork to end it.
8.reversed:
The eighth house with this card reversed can mean an ending that won't finish. The relationship's over in every way except the practical one. You still share a bank account with an ex, or a debt, or a lease. Or you're still physically close to someone long after the closeness in other ways has gone. Water on water keeps the feelings stirred up, and the trine makes it very easy to slide back in.

Money is usually where it shows, in a shared cost you resent and keep paying, and in intimacy that's become a way of avoiding a conversation. Old grief may resurface, asking to be dealt with properly. Pick one tie, emotional or financial, that you've been meaning to close, and set a date for closing it.

9.upright:
Belief, study, long-distance travel and the big questions about what life's for all sit in the ninth house. This card here says you're outgrowing a belief or a teacher or a way of making sense of things. Maybe a faith you were raised in. Maybe a set of ideas you signed up to at twenty and still quote, though you've stopped agreeing with them. Maybe a degree you've half finished, or a dream of living overseas that's gone quiet in you.

Pisces squares Sagittarius, this house's natural sign, so there's friction, and water and fire don't sit easily together. The ninth house wants to be sure and optimistic, and this card is sad and uncertain. What they do share is Jupiter, which rules Sagittarius and, in the traditional system, Pisces too, so both are looking for meaning. The difference is that this card looks for it by walking away from what you've been told. You may feel a bit lost without the framework you've leaned on, and that feeling is a normal part of changing your mind about something big. The Sun has its joy here, and searching for your own answers is exactly what this house is good at.

With study, you might drop a course that no longer leads anywhere you want to go. With belief, you might step back from a group or a teacher, quietly. With travel, a trip that used to be about escape could turn into one about looking for something. Read one book by someone who disagrees with what you used to believe.
9.reversed:
Without a direction, the search can go round in circles when this card is reversed in the ninth house. You've let go of an old belief and haven't found anything to put in its place, so you move between ideas, teachers, courses and trips without settling on any of them. Fire and water are opposed here, and they leave you restless without getting you anywhere.

Or you cling to the old belief well past the point where you hold it, because giving it up would upset people you love. It shows up in study you've abandoned, in travel plans that never happen, and in arguments about big ideas that are really about something personal. Choose one question you actually care about and stay with it for a good while before looking for another.

10.upright:
Saturn is the natural ruler of the tenth house, and it's the planet behind the Eight of Cups, so this card is on home turf in your career and speaks with a lot of authority there. The tenth is your working life seen from outside, the role you're known for, the title on your email signature, your reputation. What the card says is usually plain. You've reached a point in your work that looks fine to everyone else and isn't feeding you any more.

That's hard to take in the house of achievement. You may have worked years to get here, and walking away feels like throwing out the investment. Saturn doesn't see it that way. It's the planet of time and of knowing when something's done, and on home ground it tends to push for a considered exit, well planned and well timed. Pisces and Capricorn, the house's natural sign, are in sextile, and water and earth help each other, so the longing in the card can be turned into practical steps. People who draw this card here usually aren't about to walk out in a huff. They're about to start planning.

At work, that might mean quietly updating your CV, talking to someone in a field you've wondered about, or booking a proper conversation with your manager. With your reputation, you might stop needing to be known for what you've always been known for. With a parent or mentor whose expectations shaped your career, it's separating what you want from what they wanted. Write down what you'd like to be known for in ten years, and set it next to the job you have.
10.reversed:
The tenth house reversed often means staying in a role you've outgrown because of what leaving would look like. You're senior, you're respected, and the thought of starting lower somewhere else is hard to bear. Saturn on home turf makes you very good at enduring, and reversed, that just means you could put up with this for years.

It can also show as leaving badly, a sudden resignation with no plan, which damages a reputation you spent years building. At work you might feel bored and anxious at once. People may notice you've stopped caring about things you used to lead. Map out the next two years in writing, in two versions, one where you stay and one where you go, and see which you'd rather live.

11.upright:
Friends, groups and hopes for the future are what the eleventh house holds. Your circle, the clubs and teams and causes you belong to, the online communities, the long-range plans you'd only admit to a close friend. The Eight of Cups here says you've grown past one of these. It might be a group that still meets for dinner and doesn't feel like yours any more. It might be a hope you've had for years and quietly stopped wanting.

Saturn is the traditional ruler of this house, so the card is on home ground here too, and it tends to handle leaving a group with some dignity. You're unlikely to storm out. The complication is the link between Pisces and Aquarius, the house's natural sign. They're next-door signs with little in common, and water and air don't naturally understand each other, so your feelings about the group and your reasons for going may not line up neatly. Jupiter has its joy in this house, so there's usually some hope left over once the old plan goes, and often a new friend or two in the gap.

With friends, you might see some people less and feel no need to explain it. With a cause or a club, it could mean stepping down from a role you've held for years. With your hopes, swapping an old goal for one that fits who you've become. List the groups you belong to and mark the ones you'd join again if you were asked for the first time.
11.reversed:
When this card is reversed in the eleventh house, you might stay in a friendship group out of habit and loyalty, turning up and feeling lonely in the middle of it. Saturn, this house's natural ruler, is good at duty, and turned over it keeps you signed up to things you've stopped believing in. Pisces and Aquarius have little in common, which makes it hard to explain what's changed.

Or you drop out of everything at once, cut off the whole group, and end up with nobody. Online, it can look like scrolling through groups and forums you've long lost interest in. A hope you've outgrown can keep you from forming a newer one. Tell one friend in the group that you've felt out of place, and see what they say back.

12.upright:
This is the card's home ground twice over. The twelfth house's natural sign is Pisces, the card's own sign, and Saturn, the card's planet, has its joy here, which is the old astrologers' way of saying it does its best work in this house. So the Eight of Cups sits very comfortably in the twelfth, and whatever it's asking of you will probably come through clearly.

The twelfth is the private back room of your life. Sleep, dreams, time alone, what you don't tell people, the habits nobody sees, and whatever spiritual practice you keep. The card here is about leaving something at that level, something that's been going on under the surface. A habit of escape, maybe, the scrolling in bed, the late-night snacking, the daydream you retreat into. A private loyalty to an old hope, or an old person. Saturn in its joy is good at quiet, disciplined change, and with water on water you'll feel the loss, for better and for too much. You may want more time alone than usual, and that's fine in this house.

With sleep, it could be a change in how you wind down, fewer screens, earlier nights, a notebook by the bed. With private habits, dropping one you've been hiding even from yourself. With a spiritual or reflective practice, leaving one that's gone dry and finding another. Give yourself a proper stretch of time alone, a whole afternoon with no plans, and notice what you reach for out of habit.
12.reversed:
In the twelfth house, the card reversed tends to mean hiding from something you should be leaving. You know an old pattern has to go, and you retreat into sleep, TV, too much time alone, anything that means you don't have to decide. Saturn has its joy in this house and could help you, but with the card upside down its discipline goes into keeping secrets.

It can show up as sleep that doesn't refresh you, a feeling of being tired for no reason, and private habits you'd rather nobody knew about. Money can drift in small hidden ways too, the subscriptions you never mention. A friend may say you've gone quiet. Pick one private habit that isn't doing you any good and tell one trusted person about it, so it's no longer only yours to carry.
